races.name: Enter ITV7 For Free Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

runners_data.name: Arc Vince
runners_data.spotlight: 23,000gns yearling; half-brother to winners Don Chicco (Italian 6f-1m Group 2; RPR 110) and Hidden Happiness (Swedish 6f 2yo); dam, unraced half-sister to smart 1m-1m2f winner Khairaat, is out of a half-sister to 1m4f Group 2 winner Maraahel; the market can guide for this son of Ubettabelieveit.

runners_data.name: Fuel The Jet
runners_data.spotlight: 75,000euros foal, 190,000euros yearling; half-brother to winners Tales Of Wisdom (7f/1m; RPR 103) and Bold Style (Listed-placed 1m; RPR 103); dam unraced half-sister to Group 1 winners Tornado Alert (German 1m2f) and Just Fine (Australian 1m4f); this son of Space Blues needs considering.

runners_data.name: High Hazard
runners_data.spotlight: 30,000euros foal, £95,000 yearling; Palace Pier colt; dam is an unraced sister to 6f winner Partitia; yard's juveniles are going well so this newcomer must enter calculations.

runners_data.name: Pikachu
runners_data.spotlight: 450,000gns yearling; closely related to 1m winner Foniska (Listed; RPR 107) and a half-brother to winners Botagoz (7f/1m; RPR 97) and Boca Queen (Canadian 7f); dam 1m-1m2f winner (Group 2; RPR 113); lots to like on paper so this son of Frankel rates an interesting newcomer.

runners_data.name: Rosberg
runners_data.spotlight: 45,000gns foal, 125,000gns yearling; half-brother to Qatari 12.5f winner Beat The Clock; dam, 1m winner (RPR 74), is a half-sister to 1m/10.6f winner Halcyon Spirit; this Palace Pier colt is in good hands and very much one to consider.

runners_data.name: Whispering Moon
runners_data.spotlight: 60,000gns foal, 100,000gns yearling; Sea The Moon colt; dam, German 1m1f winner, is a half-sister to German Oaks winner Well Timed; appeals on pedigree so he is another newcomer to consider.

runners_data.name: Alfred Wallace
runners_data.spotlight: 14-1, shaped well when a debut fifth of ten in novice at Ascot (6f, good to firm) 22 days ago, running on late; this son of Dubawi seems sure to take a step forward over this longer trip; big shout.

runners_data.name: Sir Sirius
runners_data.comment: 350,000gns Starman colt; one of two for Kevin Ryan, whose 2yos have started well
runners_data.spotlight: 11-1 and very green when a never-dangerous ninth of 15 on his debut in novice at York (6f, good) 17 days ago; this son of Starman fetched 350,000gns as a yearling and it would come as no surprise to see him take a sizeable step forward.

runners_data.name: Leave The Bag In
runners_data.comment: Not really bred to be an early type; yard also responsible for Clash Of Hearts
runners_data.spotlight: 16-1 and green, made an encouraging start when eighth of 15 in novice at York (6f, good) 17 days ago, going on well at the finish; this Cotai Glory colt is capable of better, especially over this longer trip.

runners_data.name: Dave's Matey
runners_data.comment: Fifth foal from a French 7.5f 2yo winner; stable runs four newcomers in this
runners_data.spotlight: 25-1 and very green when 13th of 15 in maiden at Redcar (6f, good) on his debut 13 days ago; this son of Invincible Army can take a step forward.

races.name: Flutter Proud To Support Young Lives Vs Cancer Handicap

runners_data.name: Big Fun
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning from 43 days off with solid course and distance form, perfectly positioned for pace collapse
runners_data.comment: Promising at two, running well in the Super Sprint when last seen; stable runs three here
runners_data.spotlight: Steadily progressive at two (bagged 5f Musselburgh maiden) and he resumed from nine months off with a good fourth of 14 over C&D last month; possibilities.

runners_data.name: Under The Radar
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who shaped like he needed the run at Haydock, better positioned with recent experience
runners_data.comment: Won at Thirsk (5f, good) last May on his second start but failed to progress subsequently
runners_data.spotlight: Landed C&D maiden last May and largely performed with credit after; shaped as if the run was needed after nine months off when fifth of eight at Haydock (5f) on his reappearance and he should strip sharper here.

runners_data.name: Dazzling Haze
runners_data.note: Prominent runner making encouraging stable debut for Cowell, 43-day break could be issue in competitive heat
runners_data.spotlight: A dual 5f winner for Simon and Ed Crisford at two; made an encouraging start for new yard after seven months off when fifth of 14 over C&D last month so enters calculations.

runners_data.name: Mighty Magnus
runners_data.note: Prominent sort who disappointed last time at Hamilton over 6f, better suited back to minimum trip
runners_data.comment: Good clear second at Ripon last month; not taken lightly despite a 4lb weights rise
runners_data.spotlight: Shaped well when second on reappearance at Ripon (6f) in April but he beat only one in 6f Hamilton handicap the following month; this fair 5.5f juvenile winner shouldn't be written off.

runners_data.name: Ambishio
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who bounced back at Southwell, likely to set strong pace from the gates
runners_data.spotlight: Gained a first win at Southwell (5f) in January and in good form until only eighth in 5f Chester handicap 23 days ago; he's the sort to bounce back.

runners_data.name: Straight Ahead
runners_data.note: Early leader returning from 162-day layoff after productive gelding operation, major fitness concern
runners_data.spotlight: Improved for being gelded and bagged a pair of 5f nurseries at Newcastle late in 2025; back from five months off here but he's still not out of things nudged up 2lb.

runners_data.name: Here Forever
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist switching from Boughey stable after 246-day absence, unknown quantity on return
runners_data.spotlight: Son of Havana Grey who improved with each of his three runs at two, landing 6f Ripon maiden in September on his final run for George Boughey; has since changed hands for 52,000gns (also gelded) and very much one to consider on his handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Noble Vow
runners_data.note: Pacey hold-up horse arriving in red-hot form with two recent wins, perfectly suited to strong early pace
runners_data.comment: Comfortably won recent Bath maiden; could be on a handy mark if things have now clicked
runners_data.spotlight: No Nay Never colt who arrives on the up, getting off the mark in 5.5f Bath maiden before coming home really strongly to follow up in 5f Haydock handicap eight days ago; up 7lb but not taken lightly in his hat-trick bid.

runners_data.name: Go Vince Go
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with useful juvenile form, better recent efforts suggest he's finding his stride
runners_data.comment: A dual C&D winner; good fourth at Chester latest so must enter calculations off same mark
runners_data.spotlight: A three-time juvenile winner (including 5f York nursery); better form in defeat this season, prominent for a long way when a very good third of 14 in 6f handicap at Hamilton two weeks ago; interesting reverting to 5f.

runners_data.name: Kinnalargy
runners_data.note: Front-running specialist who needed his comeback run at York 16 days ago, fitter second time out
runners_data.comment: Showed good pace when fourth in 6f nursery at Doncaster when last seen; gelded since
runners_data.spotlight: A fairly useful 5f juvenile winner; gelded/off eight months and shaped as if the run was needed when 13th in 5f York handicap 16 days ago; no surprise to see him play a prominent role here.

runners_data.name: Sands Of Josepi
runners_data.note: Another front-runner who's struggled since winning at Southwell, likely to contribute to strong gallop
runners_data.comment: Disappointing in sole nursery but could settle better in first-time hood on reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Gained a first win in 5f Southwell novice in November but has failed to kick on, hooded when a hanging sixth of eight in 5f Haydock handicap on his return eight days ago; more is needed.

runners_data.name: Explosive Finnish
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with two encouraging thirds this season, suits the likely strong pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Creditable thirds this spring in his first two handicaps and he's one to consider
runners_data.spotlight: Son of Pinatubo who has shaped with promise when third on both his starts this season, not enjoying a clear passage when third of 14 in 5f Beverley handicap 27 days ago; a likely player off an unchanged mark.

runners_data.name: Henrythenate
runners_data.note: Backmarker switching to Morris stable, claiming jockey reduces weight but adds inexperience factor
runners_data.spotlight: Kickstarted 2026 with a pair of 5f wins at Lingfield; not in such good form subsequently for Stuart Williams but made an encouraging start for his new stable with fifth in 5f Chester handicap last time; no forlorn hope.

races.paceDynamic: Kinnalargy, Ambishio, Straight Ahead and Sands Of Josepi will ensure a strong early gallop over this sprint trip, with multiple confirmed front-runners unlikely to give each other an easy time. The pace will be testing from the start, potentially creating carnage in the final furlong as the early leaders feel the pinch. This searching gallop will set up the race perfectly for the hold-up horses and prominent racers with tactical speed - Big Fun, Here Forever, Noble Vow and Explosive Finnish are all ideally positioned to benefit from the pace collapse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Profits
scenarios.trigger: If the early leaders go too fast and tie up in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The strong pace will find out the front-runners, allowing the patient rides to come with late runs when it matters most. Noble Vow and Big Fun are perfectly suited to this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one horse can sit just off the pace and avoid the early speed battle
scenarios.body: Under The Radar or Go Vince Go can position themselves ideally behind the leaders before striking in the final 100 yards. This allows them to benefit from the pace without getting embroiled in the early fireworks.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but not suicidal and one leader has enough left
scenarios.body: Ambishio or Kinnalargy could potentially lead throughout if they can moderate the early fractions slightly. The winner would need to be tough enough to withstand late challenges while maintaining their advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If the leaders go far too fast and multiple horses tie up dramatically
scenarios.body: The entire complexion changes with a messy finish where any horse positioned mid-pack could emerge from the carnage. This chaotic scenario could throw up an outsider who avoided trouble completely.

watchPoints.text: Straight Ahead faces major fitness test after 162 days off despite his early pace-setting tendencies
Kinnalargy needed his comeback run badly at York and could improve significantly with that run under his belt
Noble Vow's recent winning form makes him the most logical beneficiary if the pace sets up as expected
Multiple front-runners Ambishio, Kinnalargy and Sands Of Josepi could create a pace meltdown scenario
Big Fun showed solid course and distance form last time and represents value in the hold-up division

races.name: Sky Bet Club Handicap

runners_data.name: Muker
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with course form who typically improves third time out each season, low weight suits
runners_data.spotlight: Multiple winner, including here; quiet this season but it was the same last campaign before he won on his third outing; handy mark.

runners_data.name: Vantheman
runners_data.note: Front-runner in good form after Hamilton win, blinkers again, will control the pace from the front
runners_data.comment: Only second go in blinkers when making all at Hamilton; possibilities under 5lb penalty
runners_data.spotlight: None too consistent but he surged back to form with a win at Hamilton (5f, good; made all) two weeks ago; that was only his second go in blinkers and he's again of interest off 4lb higher.

runners_data.name: Al Hussar
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in good nick but tight handicap mark leaves little margin for error off this rating
runners_data.comment: In good form over 5f, including close second last weekend; player if as effective at 6f
runners_data.spotlight: Running well over 5f before another respectable show over 6f at York last week; little margin for error off this mark but remains in good nick.

runners_data.name: Equity Law
runners_data.note: Prominent runner on useful mark who travelled well here 15 days ago before fading late
runners_data.comment: Back to last winning mark and arrives after close third over C&D; in the mix once more
runners_data.spotlight: Useful mark and was bang there in Kinetic Force's race here earlier this month; below that level back here 15 days ago but again he travelled well for a long way and he's still in good form.

runners_data.name: King's Call
runners_data.note: Prominent style but concerning recent form shows tendency to fade badly in the finish
runners_data.comment: Generally struggled for this yard last summer; down in the weights but not  a solid option
runners_data.spotlight: Eighth of 24 in a 5f handicap at Royal Ascot last season but he's finished out the back in his subsequent runs; bit risky.

runners_data.name: Mondammej
runners_data.note: Hold-up veteran returning from 211-day break with history of awkward behaviour
runners_data.comment: Went close over C&D last month but not in same form when fourth here five days later
runners_data.spotlight: Veteran with a mind of his own and refused to leave the parade ring on last intended start in November; however, perfectly capable of a big run off this mark and he's gone well fresh in the past.

runners_data.name: Mon Na Slieve
runners_data.note: Front-runner from same stable as winner, close up behind Vantheman last time, flatter track may help
runners_data.comment: Inconsistent front-runner; on a competitive mark if he's on a going day though
runners_data.spotlight: Inconsistent front-runner but was close up behind Vantheman at Hamilton and this flatter track could suit better; respected.

runners_data.name: Far Above The Law
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won last time at Ascot, 6lb rise may be harsh for this stronger field
runners_data.spotlight: Did well over 6f for Alice Haynes and coped fine with the drop back to 5f at Ascot where he was prominent throughout and prevailed by just over a length; this 6lb higher mark isn't beyond him.

runners_data.name: Copper Knight
runners_data.note: Prominent 12-year-old veteran with excellent course record but coming off Class 2 defeat
runners_data.spotlight: Grand old veteran who can be forgiven his defeat in a Class 2 at York last time, having won at this level the time before at Beverley (2lb lower); had 119 races and yet this is his first visit here.

runners_data.name: Montezuma
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who wasn't suited by 6f trip last time, better back at minimum distance
runners_data.comment: No worries about the return to 6f in another big field and may yet be capable of better
runners_data.spotlight: Competitive over 5f at Musselburgh this spring and wasn't at his best at Hamilton two weeks ago (6f); capable of bouncing back.

runners_data.name: Spring Is Sprung
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who faded behind Vantheman but moved well for long way, wide draw
runners_data.comment: As good as ever on Tapeta lately; returns to turf 3lb above his highest winning mark
runners_data.spotlight: Strike-rate of 8-34 includes five turf wins; seventh behind Vantheman at Hamilton 14 days ago but moved well for a long way before fading late on.

runners_data.name: Kinetic Force
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won over course and distance last time, up 4lb but remains well-treated
runners_data.comment: Two good runs for Ruth Carr this spring; up in class but should make another bold bid
runners_data.spotlight: Has made a good start for Ruth Carr and emerged from midfield to edge home over C&D a month ago; on that run and past exploits, he remains on a useful mark up 4lb.

runners_data.name: American Bay
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with course form, new cheekpieces may provide needed improvement
runners_data.spotlight: One of his two wins came over C&D and was a close fifth here a month ago, backing up two good runs on the AW; possibilities, especially should the new cheekpieces give him a lift.

runners_data.name: Acrisius
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 46-day break, won off lower mark but may have been unsuited by soft ground recently
runners_data.comment: Won on good ground last July; perhaps unsuited by softer going in two runs since
runners_data.spotlight: Won off 4lb lower at Chester (5f, good) last July and perhaps unsuited by softer going in two starts since; only had 12 races and couldn't dismiss.

runners_data.name: Woohoo
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who won last time out, extreme wide draw but light weight compensates
runners_data.comment: Won four early last summer, including over C&D, and again at Musselburgh on latest start
runners_data.spotlight: Fifth career win when beating seven rivals at Musselburgh (5f, good) and she got behind before staying on in Vantheman's race at Hamilton; drawn on the wing but has a big run in her.

runners_data.name: Changeofmind
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse stepping up in grade after Pontefract win, 6lb rise looks workable
runners_data.comment: Beaten 17 times since winning first two starts; drops in class on ground that should suit
runners_data.spotlight: Up in grade after winning a Class 5 at Pontefract (5f, good to soft) but had dropped to a tempting mark; wouldn't count the 6lb rise against him.

runners_data.name: I'm Next
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who disappointed in Class 2 but remains on competitive mark for this grade
runners_data.comment: Improved this year; further progress not ruled out, but necessary with step up in grade
runners_data.spotlight: Dropped away in a Class 2 at York last time but had previously looked a 4yo on the upgrade and remains on a competitive mark; makes the shortlist.

runners_data.name: Vince L'Amour
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with inconsistent recent form despite Ripon win, hard to trust
runners_data.comment: Won from the rail draw at Ripon and a 6lb rise looks plenty as he goes back up in class
runners_data.spotlight: Recent Ripon winner but poor on either side of that and he has become hard to predict.

races.paceDynamic: Vantheman is the only confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from the gates, with Mon Na Slieve, Far Above The Law, Equity Law and Spring Is Sprung likely to track him in the early stages. This creates a sustainable pace rather than a burn-up, as Vantheman won't be pressured for the lead and can control the fractions. With 18 runners spread across the track and no genuine speed battle up front, the pace will be even rather than frantic, allowing those with finishing kicks from off the pace to get involved. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses and those comfortable racing from midfield, as they can pick off the pace-setters in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Favours Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Vantheman dictates moderate fractions without early pressure
scenarios.body: The even gallop allows hold-up horses to conserve energy and unleash finishing kicks, while the prominent runners get picked off late. Closers with the best turn of foot will surge past the tiring leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Early Pace Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If Mon Na Slieve or Far Above The Law challenge Vantheman early
scenarios.body: The increased tempo stretches the field and creates opportunities for prominent runners with stamina to capitalize. Those tracking the pace can strike when the leaders tie up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Vantheman Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Vantheman gets uncontested fractions and kicks clear
scenarios.body: His Hamilton form suggests he's in prime condition and the lack of early pressure allows him to save enough for a strong finish. The pace-setters dominate with closers arriving too late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide Draw Advantage
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses and wide-drawn runners get clear runs
scenarios.body: Horses drawn away from the main action avoid traffic problems and can make smooth late progress. The lack of early pace means stamina becomes crucial in the final stages.

watchPoints.text: Vantheman could steal this if he gets uncontested fractions and no serious pace pressure materializes early
King's Call has shown a concerning pattern of fading badly and looks risky despite decent early form
Mondammej returning after 211 days and previous refusal to leave parade ring makes him unreliable
Watch Mon Na Slieve's early positioning as he could provide the pace pressure needed to set this up for closers
Muker typically needs his early runs but has strong course form and could outrun odds if ready to strike

races.name: Sky Bet Extra Places Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Great Bedwyn
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist suited by the likely steady pace, but winless in 13 starts despite recent placed efforts suggests he may lack that final gear
runners_data.comment: Won this last year off 4lb higher; could bounce back (from latest start) with e-w claims
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten on his last 13 starts going back to last May but he's been a good second on two of his last three starts, most recently in a big field at York (1m4f, good) this month; every chance he'll again be bang there.

runners_data.name: Penzance
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who can sit handy and benefit if the pace quickens, recent Lingfield second suggests he's found his mark
runners_data.comment: A smart performer in his time, but well below form in last two starts; look elsewhere
runners_data.spotlight: Having dropped down the weights he returned to form when runner-up off today's mark at Lingfield (1m4f, AW) recently on his second start for this yard; however, he's 5-22 on AW as opposed to 0-11 on Flat turf, and needs to back up that latest performance now back on grass.

runners_data.name: Cabrera
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 71-day break may need this run despite being well-handicapped on 2023 form
runners_data.spotlight: Ran just once last year (last April) and also unable to pose a threat on her comeback at Newcastle this March; however, she's on a handy mark on her 2024 exploits and may be able to rediscover that form at some point.

runners_data.name: Optician
runners_data.note: Strong stayer whose recent Southwell fourth suggests fitness is returning, but poor turf record remains a concern
runners_data.spotlight: 0-14 on turf (5-19 on AW) but he ran well when he last tackled grass in summer 2024; returned from some time off with promising fourth at Southwell (1m3f, AW) last month and can be in the mix if building on that effort.

runners_data.name: Brielle
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with 204-day absence who won't be fully tuned up for this return despite having ability
runners_data.spotlight: Won a novice at Hamilton (1m, good) last July and back on the scoresheet at Ayr (1m2f, good to soft) in September on third handicap start; failed to kick on subsequently but had excuses for those two runs; there can be be optimism that 1m4f will suit; could go well in first-time tongue-tie on return.

runners_data.name: Fast Fred
runners_data.note: Reliable hold-up performer whose recent Hamilton disappointment can be excused, suits this longer trip
runners_data.spotlight: Disappointing behind Letsbefrank at Hamilton a fortnight ago but in good form otherwise this year, with two close seconds sandwiching a win at Musselburgh (1m4f, good); no surprise if he bounces back with a big performance.

runners_data.name: Serenity Blue
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who can dictate terms but may be vulnerable to closers if pace stays steady throughout
runners_data.spotlight: Two novice wins last May/June (1m2f, good to firm) and back on track when third in handicap at Kempton (1m4f, AW) last month; down the field at Ascot (1m4f, good to firm) since on first run since being gelded but this 4yo remains lightly raced and is not written off.

runners_data.name: Spanish Hustle
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose Hamilton reappearance can be ignored after pulling hard, better with settling
runners_data.comment: Easily best known at Hamilton but needed at least his first run back in previous seasons
runners_data.spotlight: Hamilton specialist who was tailed off there on his reappearance a fortnight ago (pulled hard); hard to fancy on the back of that but it may have got the freshness out of him and he's on his last winning mark; not a forlorn hope on his first visit here.

runners_data.name: Letsbefrank
runners_data.note: In-form hold-up horse whose recent wins under Lauren Young show he's thriving, dangerous from off the pace
runners_data.spotlight: He's reappeared in rude health this year with wins under Lauren Young at Musselburgh (1m4f, good) and Hamilton (1m3f, good); beat bang-in-form stablemate last time and a 5lb higher mark might not stop this course winner.

runners_data.name: Valley Of Flowers
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who's been consistent but hasn't shown the same level in 2024, lowest weight helps
runners_data.spotlight: Consistent last July-September and nicely treated on that form; however, she hasn't been at the same level on her two outings this year.

runners_data.name: Eroico
runners_data.note: Prominent runner making handicap debut who could improve for this step up in trip and stable switch
runners_data.spotlight: Ran in five maidens in Ireland for Noel Meade, finishing second on the final occasion (1m4f, heavy); has also shown promise on good ground; she could improve for last month's stable/seasonal debut at Musselburgh (1m4f, good) but was soundly beaten and others have more pressing claims; a hood goes on.

runners_data.name: Damascus Steel
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with AW wins but returning from 58-day break and unproven on turf makes him vulnerable
runners_data.comment: In good form in recent months including a win over C&D; respected on stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: Two 1m4f AW wins last winter for Denis Quinn and respectable fifth of 15 at Lingfield (1m4f, AW) last month on sole run for John Ryan; however, it's a long time since he ran well on turf and has something to prove back on grass; stable debut.

races.paceDynamic: Serenity Blue will lead with Spanish Hustle and Eroico providing early company from prominent positions, creating a sustainable gallop in the first half mile. The presence of multiple hold-up horses (Great Bedwyn, Optician, Brielle, Fast Fred, Letsbefrank, Valley Of Flowers, Damascus Steel) means the front-runners won't face early pressure, allowing them to dictate terms through measured sectionals. This sets up a tactical affair where the pace will gradually increase from the three-furlong pole as the field compresses. The race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can time their runs from off the pace, as they'll have the tactical advantage of racing into a steady tempo with enough left in the tank for a finishing kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners maintain control without pressure and the pace stays steady until the final three furlongs
scenarios.body: The large contingent of closers will have perfect conditions to unleash finishing kicks, with the race becoming a sprint from the two-furlong marker. Hold-up specialists with proven stamina at this trip will have the tactical edge over those who've led throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Kick Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Serenity Blue and Spanish Hustle increase the tempo from halfway and stretch the field
scenarios.body: The early leaders will exploit their positional advantage by gradually winding up the pace, making it difficult for hold-up horses to close the gap. Those racing handy to the pace will benefit from avoiding traffic problems in a strung-out finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo remains pedestrian throughout with all hold-up horses waiting too long to make their moves
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy sprint where those with natural speed will have the edge over pure stayers. Horses who can quicken sharply despite being positioned off the pace will benefit from the lack of early pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Wire Win
scenarios.trigger: If Serenity Blue faces no serious challenges and is allowed to coast in front throughout
scenarios.body: The leader will have too much in reserve having faced no pressure, allowing her to kick clear when the closers finally make their moves. This scenario requires the hold-up horses to leave their runs too late against a savvy front-runner.

watchPoints.text: Serenity Blue breaks fast and gets an easy lead - if unopposed early she could steal a march on the field
Great Bedwyn and Letsbefrank both positioned close together in running as both need clear runs from off the pace
Spanish Hustle settles properly after pulling hard last time - his chances depend entirely on rider control
Fast Fred's position at halfway will reveal his chance as he needs to be within striking distance to utilise his finishing kick
The pace through the first half-mile will determine whether this becomes a stamina test or sprint finish

races.name: Sky Bet Price Boosts Handicap

runners_data.name: Toyotomi
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 23 days off with gelding operation, needs to overcome wide draw and settle properly
runners_data.spotlight: Having been gelded he made a promising reappearance at Newcastle (6f, AW) last month; failed to build on that when sixth at Ascot (6f, good) but he got upset in the stalls; well handicapped on his French form up to last July and he's not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Russet Gold
runners_data.note: Closer winless in 20 starts but showing promise for new yard, difficult to trust despite ability
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten on his last 20 starts going back to June 2023 but he's shown promise in fifth this spring on his first two starts for this yard, most recently behind a couple of these in a big field at York (6f, good); he continues to edge down the weights and might not be far away.

runners_data.name: Strike Red
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose York effort can be forgiven due to high draw, proven at this level when getting right run
runners_data.spotlight: Soundly beaten behind Dark Thirty and others at York (6f, good) last time but his high draw proved to be a negative; won at Leicester (6f, good to firm) two starts ago and he could bounce back today and be involved.

runners_data.name: Annaf
runners_data.note: Class act down to dangerous mark but needs to rediscover Group 3 form after moderate recent efforts
runners_data.spotlight: Group 3 winner at Ascot (6f, soft) last October and he's versatile ground-wise; down to a dangerous mark but he hasn't been at the top of his game on his four runs this year, in handicaps on the last two occasions, and he needs to turn things around in a first-time tongue-tie and reapplied cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Dark Thirty
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in great form after York win, proven course performer who handles this trip perfectly
runners_data.comment: Yet to shine for new yard but he's 1lb lower than when second of 16 in this last year
runners_data.spotlight: Returned to form to win big-field handicap at York (6f, good) this month on third stable start, going one better than in the same race 12 months previously; a 6lb rise shouldn't be enough to prevent another big run.

runners_data.name: Al Shabab Storm
runners_data.note: Natural front runner who ran well for long way at Chester despite wide draw, returns after 25 days
runners_data.spotlight: Finished down the field on stable/seasonal debut at Chester (7.5f) this month but that doesn't tell the full story as he ran well for a long way from his wide draw and was hampered late on; he's dropped to an attractive mark and is just the type his new trainer does very well with.

runners_data.name: Eternal Sunshine
runners_data.note: Prominent type with perfect 3-3 course record returning to happy hunting ground after hat-trick last year
runners_data.comment: Progressive last season and ran really well over C&D last October; yet to shine this term
runners_data.spotlight: Completed a hat-trick last August/September and she's capable of going close off her current mark if at her best; she's 3-3 here and perhaps the return to Thirsk will trigger a revival, but it very much needs to as she's not shone on her three outings this season.

runners_data.name: Fluorescence
runners_data.note: Forward-going sort returning from 252-day break but showed good form when fresh previously
runners_data.spotlight: Made it three wins from his five starts when landing a handicap at Redcar (5f, good to firm) last August; her two other wins came at 6f; returned to form when staying on for fourth of 14 at Southwell (5f, AW) last September when last seen and the return to 6f could be a good move on her comeback.

runners_data.name: Milford
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from wind surgery with decent form last season, interesting despite long absence
runners_data.spotlight: 0-14 since debut win in May 2024 but he often ran well in some quality handicaps last season; returns on a competitive mark having had wind surgery; could have a part to play if fully tuned up.

runners_data.name: Manila Scouse
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with course and distance win last July, building on recent Hamilton third
runners_data.comment: 2lb below his last successful mark and has won here before; David Allan on Vince L'Amour
runners_data.spotlight: His last win came over C&D last July (good; off 1lb higher) and he stayed on for a close third at Hamilton (5f, good) a fortnight ago; could build on that latest performance now back up in trip; firmly in calculations.

runners_data.name: Sir Yoshi
runners_data.note: Hold-up type struggling since yard switch but on competitive mark based on best Irish form
runners_data.spotlight: He's on a competitive mark on last season's best form for David Marnane but he was well beaten on his stable debut at York last October and it was the same outcome there this month on his return; he has plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Fandom
runners_data.note: Closer back in good form with third to Dark Thirty at York, well-placed off current mark
runners_data.spotlight: Globetrotter who has had mixed fortunes across his career but he was back on song when third of 22 to Dark Thirty at York (6f, good) this month on his second stable start; he can be in the mix if confirming that promise.

runners_data.name: Yes I'm Mali
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in excellent form with course win and York second, just 8 days since last run
runners_data.comment: Thirsk win for new yard last month and this easier than Newbury Class 2 last weekend
runners_data.spotlight: Won over C&D (good) last month on second stable start; midfield finish at Newbury (6f, good) next time before 1l second of 20 at York (6f, good) last Saturday; he could still have more to offer for this yard; respected.

runners_data.name: Gangsta Man
runners_data.note: Prominent type whose Newmarket effort forgiven after failing to settle, better at shorter trips
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten at Newmarket last month (7f, good; has won at that trip in the past) but he failed to settle and didn't look at home on the track; prior to that he kept on strongly to go very close at Musselburgh (5f, soft) on his stable debut and he remains one to be interested in.

races.paceDynamic: Al Shabab Storm will lead with Dark Thirty, Manila Scouse and Eternal Sunshine prominent early, creating a sustainable gallop over this straight 6f track. The pace will be testing but not excessive with these four sharing duties through the early stages. Gangsta Man and Fluorescence may also press forward from their draws, adding to the tempo. This sets up perfectly for the strong contingent of hold-up horses who can settle off the pace and unleash late kicks - the race shape clearly favours closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Closers dominate finish
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is honest but not breakneck with the front division staying together
scenarios.body: The prominent horses will soften each other up through the middle stages, allowing the hold-up brigade to sweep past in the final furlong with their superior finishing kicks. Horses like Yes I'm Mali, Fandom and Annaf can time their runs to perfection.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front runners persist
scenarios.trigger: If Al Shabab Storm and Dark Thirty break clear and the pace becomes moderate
scenarios.body: The leaders get an easy time of it through soft fractions and have enough left to resist the late challengers in a blanket finish. Dark Thirty's recent York form gives him the edge in a sustained drive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent horses prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and burns up both leaders and closers
scenarios.body: The horses tracking the early pace in fourth to sixth positions inherit the race as both extreme pace styles suffer. This tactical position allows them to kick when others are stopping.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and longshot
scenarios.trigger: If there's significant early pace pressure causing the field to fragment
scenarios.body: A messy early gallop creates gaps and traffic problems that favour an outsider getting a dream run through or a horse coming from an impossible position. The form book goes out the window.

watchPoints.text: Yes I'm Mali has had three runs in 22 days including last Saturday at York which could leave him vulnerable despite good recent form
Al Shabab Storm needs to reproduce his Chester effort where he led for long way from wide draw - any early pressure could compromise him
Strike Red carries 3lb claimer Warren Fentiman which suggests connections are serious about his chances after disappointing York run
Watch for any market moves on Fluorescence returning from 252 days off - yard has decent record with returning runners
Annaf drops significantly in class from Group level but hasn't shown his best form in four runs this season

races.name: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Elysian Flame
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with proven 2m ability but 28 days off and faces serious traffic dangers in a congested field
runners_data.spotlight: Smart staying handicapper for Mick and David Easterby in 2021 when competitive at some of the top meetings; only his second run since when winning over 2m at Beverley (good to soft; 2lb higher today) in April, while 1m5f helps to explain his last of five at Hamilton four weeks ago; not dismissed.

runners_data.name: Laafy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 407-day break with poor trainer form, hard to trust despite past class
runners_data.spotlight: Formerly with Sir Michael Stoute, smart over 1m4f in 2020 when usually visored; absent for 1373 days before last season and staged a partial recovery when tried in cheekpieces at Musselburgh (1m6f) on second run back, admittedly in only eighth of 14 (beaten about 5l); dropped another 6lb since but also absent another 407 days.

runners_data.name: Artisan Dancer
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits but poor turf record (1-19) and 14 days since last run creates fitness doubts
runners_data.spotlight: Industrious and dependable sort at 1m6f-2m2f but turf strike-rate is 1-19; not discredited on latest start (1m5f) but others are preferred.

runners_data.name: Almuhit
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who thrived front-running in small fields but faces much tougher tactical test here
runners_data.comment: Stepping back up from 1m6f should suit but this race may also prove too tough
runners_data.spotlight: Rediscovered the knack for new stable last year, including two front-running wins over 2m in four-runner Flat races and two places when the action got more competitive; returned to some hurdles form on last two outings in that sphere; a lesser show on Musselburgh Flat in between was over 1m6f but this race may also prove too tough.

runners_data.name: Mountain Road
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose style perfectly suits this pace shape, building on recent promise for in-form Jim Goldie
runners_data.spotlight: 4-15 for David Simcock; four runs for current yard, absent 582 days before this season's, in which he showed that significant ability remains; needs to build on those performances but going back up from the 1m5f of last two outings should suit and he continues down the weights; case can be made.

runners_data.name: Hermetic
runners_data.note: Prominent French import with soft ground wins, headgear change could unlock improvement on good ground
runners_data.spotlight: Dual soft-ground winner (1m4f/2m) in France last autumn, from just four races there; picked up for 105,000euros in November and put up a bold show when fourth of 17 at York (1m4f, good) 18 days ago; stuck to his task at 20-1 that day and looks a strong candidate if that run has brought him on.

runners_data.name: St Faz
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in excellent form with four wins this year, but stepping up significantly in class
runners_data.spotlight: Usually races prominently; won four of his six starts for new yard this year, including when returned to turf for eight-runner race at Musselburgh (2m, good) in April; has excuses for the two defeats, on latest occasion fifth of 17 in the 2m2f Chester Plate despite the work he had to do to front-run from wide draw; one to note.

runners_data.name: Arrange
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare 15lb below last winning mark but Martin Todhunter stable in poor form recently
runners_data.comment: Twice 2nd over 2m from five visits here; others seem to be banging on the door more loudly
runners_data.spotlight: Last won in August 2024; placed in three of eight starts last term and it was a hot race in which she was well beaten at York (40-1) on 2026 return; 15lb below peak mark but others seem to be banging on the door more loudly.

runners_data.name: Anniversary
runners_data.note: Front-running blinkered four-year-old who flopped as favourite last time but has tactical speed to dominate
runners_data.spotlight: Blinkered on four of his last five starts; flopped when 5-4 favourite behind Elysian Flame at Beverley (2m, good to soft) in April but this month's second of nine at Salisbury (1m6f, good; made most and rallied well) was his closest finish since 2yo and gives some renewed hope.

runners_data.name: Pole Star
runners_data.note: Prominent runner helped by first-time visor at Newmarket, back in calculations after earlier letdowns
runners_data.spotlight: Won two 1m6f handicaps last term; back-to-form third with a first-time visor at Newmarket (1m6f) four weeks ago, so he re-enters calculations despite earlier lesser efforts over 2m2f and 2m.

runners_data.name: New York Minute
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose headgear helped on AW but unproven on turf in similar company
runners_data.spotlight: Headgear helped on AW last September-December, including for 1m6f/2m hat-trick; peak form was not repeated this year, including in two small fields this spring but they were at 1m3f/1m4f; returning to 2m should be a big help but none of his turf form (five races) approaches this mark.

runners_data.name: Minstrel Knight
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 245-day break including jumping career, fitness major concern
runners_data.spotlight: Ran creditably for minor honours in two (1m5f/2m2f) of his four starts in last year's Flat campaign and won novice hurdles in December and January when last seen; however, although he won on good ground two years ago, his record since has been dominated by achievements on softer.

runners_data.name: Treasure Islands
runners_data.note: Front-running four-year-old who made all at Ripon, improving rapidly and 10 days fresh
runners_data.spotlight: Improved for the step up in trip when making all at Ripon (2m, good) late last month on his second handicap start; not discredited when second on soft ground at Haydock (2m) ten days ago; needs to resume progress but that might be possible for this lightly raced 4yo.

runners_data.name: Gibside
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won Chester Plate off higher mark but form tailing off in recent starts
runners_data.comment: Well handicapped but needs to leave his three efforts this season a long way behind him
runners_data.spotlight: Strong finish from rear secured the Chester Plate (2m2f, good) last May off 3lb higher and he also won over 1m4f on soft at Catterick in October; needs to leave his four efforts this season a long way behind him, however.

races.paceDynamic: Anniversary and Treasure Islands will contest the early lead, with Anniversary likely to prevail given his stronger front-running credentials and Rossa Ryan's tactical awareness. Six horses (Elysian Flame, Almuhit, Hermetic, St Faz, Pole Star, Minstrel Knight, Gibside) want prominent positions, creating serious traffic problems and a bunched field approaching the home turn. The honest gallop set by the leaders will stretch out the field in the final three furlongs, but the prominent congestion means several fancied runners will find trouble. This race shape strongly favours either the confirmed front-runner who escapes the melee or hold-up horses who can find clear water late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Anniversary or Treasure Islands get uncontested leads and kick clear
scenarios.body: The winner avoids all traffic problems by being in front throughout, while the prominent brigade gets tangled up behind. Anniversary has the class edge but Treasure Islands showed improved stamina at Ripon and could steal this at bigger odds.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion creates a cavalry charge finish
scenarios.body: The early pace and midrace bunching sets up perfectly for horses held up out the back to find clear runs. Mountain Road and Arrange have the tactical speed to capitalize when others are still trying to find racing room.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Escape Artist
scenarios.trigger: If one prominent runner breaks clear from the pack 2-3 furlongs out
scenarios.body: Hermetic or St Faz uses their tactical speed to break from the congested prominent group before the sprint. The winner gets first run on the leaders while others are still stuck behind horses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders weaken dramatically in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The honest gallop becomes too much for the front pair, creating a messy finish where any of the prominent horses can grab it. Form and class matter most when tactical advantage is negated by the collapse.

watchPoints.text: Watch for Anniversary and Treasure Islands to dictate terms early - if either gets soft lead they could prove unstoppable
Monitor the prominent bunch (Almuhit, Hermetic, St Faz, Pole Star) for traffic problems approaching the home turn
Check if Mountain Road and Arrange get clean runs from the back - their hold-up style could be perfectly suited
Observe Minstrel Knight's fitness after 245-day break including hurdle wins - stamina might not last
Look for Hermetic to show improved form with good ground debut for Ian Williams after French soft wins

races.name: Sky Bet Build A Bet Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Bintaziza
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strong AW form but turf debut creates question mark despite obvious class
runners_data.comment: Justified favouritism at Newcastle in good style last month; big player despite penalty
runners_data.spotlight: Won on debut at Newcastle (1m, AW) in April and again had something to spare when following up at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW); she has the potential to be better than her opening mark and is one to consider.

runners_data.name: Thaluna
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse ideally suited to this pace setup with proven good going form
runners_data.comment: Came up short in Listed race on final 2yo start; lightly raced and in good hands
runners_data.spotlight: Won 2yo novice at York (6f, good) last October on second start; mid-division in Listed race later that month and reappeared with good second on handicap debut at Newmarket (7f, good to firm); stayed on well last time and this step up to 1m could prompt further improvement; lots to like.

runners_data.name: Thankfully
runners_data.note: Prominent style fits the race shape perfectly and recent Beverley win shows current form
runners_data.spotlight: Promising third at Sandown (7f, soft) last August on the first of her two 2yo starts and reappeared with win in a maiden at Beverley last month (8.4f, good to soft; unraced on softer); she has a useful pedigree and is in good hands to progress; possible player on handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Perfect Part
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who could benefit if prominent traffic materializes as expected
runners_data.comment: 0-14 since winning debut; never a threat on latest start and now tried in headgear
runners_data.spotlight: She's been a promising fourth on two of her three starts this season, at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) in March and here (7f, good) a fortnight ago in first-time cheekpieces (retained); might not be far away.

runners_data.name: Renewal
runners_data.note: Prominent type returning from 239-day break which raises serious fitness concerns
runners_data.spotlight: Record of 4232 in novice/maiden events on turf and again ran well when runner-up on handicap debut at Newcastle (1m2f, AW) last October; shaped on that latest outing as though the drop back in trip may be a positive and this unexposed 4yo could have a big part to play on her reappearance.

runners_data.name: Mandarin Spirit
runners_data.note: Front runner who may struggle to see out 1m after recent disappointing reappearance
runners_data.comment: Won at Thirsk; stiff task in Rockel at Newmarket so remains with potential on h'cap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Won a maiden here (7f, good) last July on second start; well beaten in Group 2 next time; she could improve for this month's reappearance sixth on handicap debut at Beverley (7.4f, good to soft) but her claims aren't compelling on the back of that.

runners_data.name: Bridget's View
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose recent form decline on turf makes her hard to fancy
runners_data.comment: Tongue-tie removed after last time; previous close fifth at Lingfield brings her into this
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Southwell (1m, AW) in December and very close fifth at Lingfield (7f, AW) in February; however, down the field on both starts since (7f, AW/good) and needs to leave those performances well behind.

runners_data.name: Annastarzy
runners_data.note: Prominent runner trapped in the danger zone for traffic with apprentice rider
runners_data.comment: Ran well in an Ascot novice ten days ago; more realistic task now handicapping
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced 3yo who appears to be on a fair mark judged on her novice form; still early days in handicaps but she was merely eighth of 12 at Windsor (1m, good to firm) three weeks ago on her first attempt in this sphere.

runners_data.name: Alessia Fernanda
runners_data.note: Prominent type with wind surgery recovery but faces tough task from congested position
runners_data.comment: Form went wrong way last season but she's had wind surgery and is on a dangerous mark
runners_data.spotlight: Two-time turf winner who returned to form with a reappearance win at Southwell (1m, AW) last month, following wind surgery; back up 4lb she remains on a workable mark and could be thereabouts.

runners_data.name: Krissy
runners_data.note: Front runner in red-hot form with two recent wins but faces stronger company today
runners_data.comment: Did it very easily at Musselburgh last Thursday; ahead of the handicapper under a penalty
runners_data.spotlight: Easily made all at Musselburgh (1m1f, good) ten days ago and did likewise under a 5lb penalty in apprentice handicap at Carlisle (1m1f, good) on Friday; unpenalised for latest win but new mark has kicked in, which is 6lb higher than that which she raced off two days ago; in a tougher race today but clearly thriving and she's a leading candidate if her fine form continues.

runners_data.name: Wetsand
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning to preferred 1m trip after disappointing shorter distance efforts
runners_data.spotlight: 1m 2yo winner last August and the return to this trip could help; kept on for fifth of eight at Yarmouth (7f, good to firm) last month, which was a step back in the right direction, but she needs another today.

runners_data.name: Geo
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with narrow recent win but faces much stronger field here
runners_data.comment: Her mark continues to slide but she needs to improve upon this season's form
runners_data.spotlight: Exploited a reduced mark when returning to form with a narrow win at Ayr (1m, good to firm) 11 days ago; this is more competitive but she's gone back up just 2lb and is not discounted.

races.paceDynamic: Mandarin Spirit and Krissy are confirmed front runners who will contest the early lead, creating an honest gallop from the start. The prominent group is dangerously congested with Bintaziza, Thankfully, Annastarzy, Alessia Fernanda and Wetsand all wanting that position, creating potential traffic problems turning for home. With only Perfect Part, Thaluna, Bridget's View and Geo as genuine hold-up horses, the pace will be solid but not destructive. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can secure clean passages and hold-up horses who can pick up the pieces late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Clean Run
scenarios.trigger: If Bintaziza or Thankfully secure clear sailing positions behind the leaders without getting trapped
scenarios.body: The honest pace allows prominent runners to stay in touch and they can kick clear when the front runners tire after 2f out. Clean passages become decisive as the congested prominent group sorts itself out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion creates traffic problems and the pace stays honest enough for closers
scenarios.body: Perfect Part and Thaluna get the perfect setup as prominent runners get squeezed and leaders tire. The hold-up horses have clear runs on the outside to mop up late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Krissy or Mandarin Spirit get uncontested leads and the prominent group fails to organize
scenarios.body: The winner gets first run on the field and maintains the advantage to the line. Recent form and fitness tells as Krissy particularly looks hard to peg back given her two recent victories.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Special
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion causes multiple horses to be denied clear runs turning in
scenarios.body: A horse who gets lucky in running or finds an unexpected gap becomes the beneficiary. Form goes out the window as positioning and fortune determine the outcome.

watchPoints.text: Watch Bintaziza, Annastarzy and Alessia Fernanda getting squeezed in the prominent traffic jam turning for home
Monitor whether Mandarin Spirit and Krissy go too fast early and set it up for the closers
Check if Thaluna and Perfect Part get the clear runs they need in the final 2f to capitalize
Observe whether Renewal shows any signs of ring-rustiness after her long absence
Notice if Thankfully can secure the ideal prominent position to avoid the expected congestion
